@@103239558 <h> Gina London : How to bring your active listening skills into a world of oversharing <p> The Communicator <p> Being a good listener can make you a better collaborator . Photo : Getty <p> Gina London <p> Yesterday at 03:30 <p> Active listening is still largely misunderstood and underappreciated . <p> I was reminded of this when I was talking to another parent the other day . Her son had just returned from his first day at a new school and was frustrated because , according to him , " the kids do n't know how to ask me back when I ask them something " . <p> I knew exactly what the mom meant . When my daughter Lulu was little , I would put her through a routine that went something like this : <p> Me : " How are you today , Lulu ? " <p> Lulu : " Fine thanks , how are you ? " <p> Me : " What was the best thing about your weekend ? " <p> Lulu : " I loved going to the park . What was the best thing about your weekend ? " <p> And on @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ to volley a follow-up question to the other party during a conversation is something that must be taught . <p> We 're simply not born interested in the lives of others . When we 're kids , the world revolves around us . Kids , of course , grow up to be adults . Adults who carry on conversations are typically more interested in sharing their ideas , experiences , opinions and advice than they are curious about what more the other person may have to say . <p> Cultivating our curiosity about others is how we can become better collaborators <p> Learning how to become a more active listener takes effort , but it 's worth it . That 's because cultivating our curiosity about others is how we can become better collaborators , provide more effective constituent and customer service and forge relationships which grow and develop and do n't stagnate and become merely transactional . <p> As pre-eminent management consultant Peter Drucker concluded in one of his seminal articles on executive leadership : " Listen first , speak last . " <h> ? How Social Media has @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ that social media is ruining society by " skewing our perception of the relative value of listening vs speaking " . <p> For instance , he points out : " Going public on an important/sensitive topic you have no domain expertise in is a transfer of value or a trade of reputation . <p> " Justin Bieber 's Instagram post ' Praying for Israel ' lost some of its force when people noticed the background image of a destroyed city was a photograph of Gaza . <p> Justin Bieber posted and later deleted this message on social media <p> " Social media has not only elevated virtue signalling to pseudo-importance , it has weaponised it . People are losing their jobs because they feel compelled to make ' statements ' . <p> " Social gave everyone a voice , but it blocked our ear canals . The more complex or painful or shocking an event , the more it behooves us to listen first , speak last . But we do n't . There 's likes to be had , and if you 're a semi-famous DJ , your fans @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ <h> ? How to relearn listening <p> So how can we resolve , like my young daughter Lulu has , to become better listeners ? <p> ? Stay focused on them <p> You know that moment when another person is talking and you begin to finish the resolution of their story or the punchline to their joke in your head ? That jump to the conclusion moment when your brain switches back to your world and how you view it . You may even begin internally constructing your own story to share before the other speaker has crossed their verbal finish line . <p> These are precisely the times I want to encourage you to try disrupting your old pattern of thinking by mentally shouting the word " focus " . I said mentally , not aloud . You might not have been listening . <p> Engage your body <p> Body language can make a huge difference <p> To help you retain that refreshed focus , whether you are meeting in person or virtual , remember to tell your face and your body to provide important indicator cues to the @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ occasionally to non-verbally demonstrate understanding , agreement or just plain , " I 'm staying with you " and following along with your delivery of your personal or professional perspective . <p> Also engage your eyes . Look at the other speaker . Do n't stare at them blankly , of course . Rather , remind yourself to sneak a glance down at your phone or over their head or shoulder at that interesting painting on the wall or whatever else may distract your attention . <p> Also tell the rest of your face to get into the act . Smile with your mouth or furrow your brow depending on the emotion of the words they are saying . <p> These mechanics might seem theatrical in nature to some of you . And they can become that way if you go overboard . But let me stress that a neutral face and body is perceived by most people as negative , disinterested or detached . <h> ? Ask a follow-up question <p> Here 's where your training on asking a follow-up question now comes importantly into play . " What @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ is almost always a better response than , " Let me tell you about me " . <p> You might have a great opinion or experience to share . But in this world of oversharing , learning to listen can be a more powerful force . <p> Stay curious , my friends . <p> Write to Gina in care of **29;176;TOOLONG <p> With corporate clients in five continents , Gina London is a premier communications strategy , structure and delivery expert . In fact , it makes it all the more valid as it is being articulated to a representative of the State whose actions are being criticised . Israel 's ambassador has been left in no doubt of Ireland 's position . <p> Expelling an ambassador , of whatever country , might make the headlines , but what do you do the next day when you seek to bring about a resolution ? Cheap soundbites do n't resolve conflicts . Diplomacy is n't always pleasant -- but it is always essential .

@@103381861 <p> After the October 7 attack , Western leaders ranging from the US President Joe Biden to British Prime Minister Rishi Sunak and French President Emmanuel Macron were quick to condemn Hamas , at times comparing it to the terrorist group Daesh . <p> But , in the 1940s , long before Palestinian resistance groups like Hamas picked up arms against the Israeli occupation , a plethora of Jewish militias were bombing and shooting dead British officials and Palestinian Arabs . <p> The Jewish groups including Haganah to Irgun , and the Stern Gang ( Lehi ) actively used terrorism against the British mandate over Palestine and to create fear among the Arab citizens . <p> " I argue that Jewish terrorism in the 1940s was both tactically and strategically significant . At the tactical level , Jewish terrorists were able to frustrate British security forces and erode their ability to control Palestine , " wrote David A. Charters , professor of military history and senior fellow of the Gregg Centre for Study of War and Society at the University of New Brunswick , Canada . <p> " That played a significant role at the strategic level in persuading @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ , created the conditions that facilitated the founding of Israel , and the consequent creation of an Arab-Palestinian diaspora , " he said in his article Jewish Terrorism and the Modern Middle East . <p> John Lois Peeke , an American military expert , also writes that Zionist terrorism was at the core of the idea of Israel . " Jewish terrorism against British and Arabs did contribute heavily to the removal of the British from Palestine , the abandonment of the League of Nations mandate and the creation of a Jewish state of Israel , " he wrote in his book Jewish-Zionist Terrorism and the Establishment of Israel . <p> Zionist terrorist groups attacked with impunity not just military targets but also civilians in the 1940s . <p> In October 1945 , Jewish underground groups simultaneously targeted colonial railways , oil refineries and police boats in Palestine . @@103490771 <h> Choose our future : 5 things to know about Science Week <p> Science Week is one of the busiest periods of the year for me . Months of work making TV shows culminates and there are so many fascinating events to attend . Here are five things you might spot during Science Week 2023 . <p> 1 . 10 Things to Know About ... is back . <p> Each year filming 10 Things to Know About I am buoyed by the researchers I meet working on some of the most important challenges facing society - from planting resilient trees , to improved ways of tracking and tackling waterborne diseases . <p> The ninth series of RT ? ' s science show is back on our screens this week with a deep dive into topics ranging from fungi to inflammatory bowel disease . <p> The first episode about trees is a strong reminder that we have all the knowledge and tools we need to fix the climate and biodiversity crisis . <p> The simple act of planting a tree sucks carbon out of the atmosphere , cleans our air , improves soil health , boosts biodiversity , helps regulate @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ way that will , if your tree keeps growing , last for decades and maybe even after you 've left the planet . <p> We need to plant a tremendous number of trees to make a dent in emissions but among the avalanche of bad news today planting a tree is a tangible , positive action that most of us can do . If you have a garden promise to plant a bare root tree this winter and watch it grow in 2024 or volunteer with a tree planting organisation like Trees Please or Hometree and spend a day laying down roots . <p> 2 . ' Tomorrow Tonight ' tomorrow night <p> Finally , someone has invented a time machine and allowed us to fast forward to 2050 . Tomorrow Tonight is a fictitious current affairs show set in November 2050 during a crunch UN summit that promises to bring in sweeping mandatory powers for climate action . On RT ? 1 on Wednesday at 9.35pm presenters Mark Little and Carla O'Brien and panels of experts will guide viewers through breaking news moments and reflect the Irish and international @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ a large team of talented people , have been working on this project throughout the year . Science is for everyone , not just budding scientists <p> Living in 2023 we are all the benefactors of scientific progress and ingenuity . Science Week is a nationwide initiative to engage the entire population on the impacts of science , technology , engineering and maths . <p> Organisers want to instil a curiosity in the next generation of scientists and engineers , but the event is not just for people with an eye on a career in STEM . Not everyone desires , or is destined , to become a scientist but we all need to navigate an increasingly complex world shaped by forces of science and engineering , therefore we need to be informed citizens to understand the consequences of new gene editing techniques or AI breakthroughs or algorithms influencing our romantic lives . <p> @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ to look and appraise robust evidence and determine how best to build the future . <p> Science is a team effort spanning the globe and we need more women in STEM . If we are going to solve the world 's problems , if we 're going to build the future , if we 're going to have science creating new cures and new technologies then we need people from diverse backgrounds with unique perspectives to create a future that serves everybody . <p> 4 . You might see a volcanic eruption <p> Worried Icelanders are keeping a close eye on real volcanoes this week , but volcanoes have a habit of popping up at Science Week events for kids . Smallies love science workshop classics like flaming hands of gas and smoke cannons . @@103707065 <h> Jennifer Horgan : Thanksgiving : It 's not easy to find a balance between morality and joy <p> In so many ways this celebration of Thanksgiving is representative of our age -- it 's meant to be a nice and pleasurable thing , but it 's really hard to feel good about it when you know the broader context <p> We live in a world where many people feel it is genuinely hard to enjoy anything without feeling guilt because we carry the pain of thousands . <p> I 'm very lucky to have American neighbours and I 'm even luckier that they 're inviting us over for Thanksgiving dinner this Saturday . <p> We went last year and it was an absolute feast of pies and sides . It was gorgeous to sit with friends from the afternoon into the evening , munching away at their multi-plated delicious treats -- turkey , stuffing , mashed potatoes , cranberry sauce , and pumpkin pie . <p> This time round , I 'm wearing stretchy pants . <p> In so many ways this celebration of Thanksgiving is representative of our age . It 's meant to be a nice @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ feel good about it when you know the broader context . <p> It 's a lovely idea to sit and give thanks and that 's how I view it . I 'm certainly not going to bring up the plight of indigenous people at my neighbours ' house . <p> Unless I 'm invited into a debate . Then , I 'm all in , but there is a time and a place for everything , and I put being kind above being right . <p> In case you do n't know already , the holiday dates back to 1621 , when the Plymouth colonists from England , and the Native American Wampanoag people , shared an autumn harvest feast . <p> The depiction of the dinner is very sunny in traditional American textbooks , not dissimilar to my neighbourhood gathering ( so long as I behave myself ) . It is presented to American children as a harmonious interaction between people from different cultures . <p> What most people do n't realise is that it did n't become an official national day of celebration until 1863 , when President @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ But people will know something about the controversy around the holiday . The first point of contention exists between Europeans . The Spanish believe that a very similar event predates the arrival of the English . In 1565 , explorer Pedro Men ? ndez de Avil ? apparently met with members of the local Timucua tribe to dinner in St Augustine , Florida . <p> But far more significant is the belief that the sunny depiction of the original event does an unforgivable disservice to indigenous people . Thanksgiving , many will argue , masks the true history of bloodshed that underpins the relationship between European settlers and Native Americans . <p> Indeed , since 1970 , protesters have gathered on the fourth Thursday of November at the top of Cole 's Hill overlooking Plymouth Rock ; this gathering marks a National Day of Mourning and similar events are held throughout the United States . <p> A different history <p> These people commemorate a very different history wherein one oppressed people , the passengers of the Mayflower -- the half of them that made it , that is -- went @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ yet even this depiction of the pilgrims is problematic . @@103901580 <p> Politics is a dirty game , at every level . Some say that it 's the art of the possible . That 's true , but it is also the art of the cynical . While we all stand on the sidelines watching the horrors in Israel and Gaza unfold , there are political opportunists using it as a smokescreen . Politicians always seek advice on when is the ' best time ' to release unwelcome news that would otherwise dominate the headlines . The answer is simple , bury it while a major story has the headlines and front pages . For the past few years both Fianna F ? il and Fine Gael senior ministers have been chomping at the bit to get Ireland aligned and supporting the move towards a European army . The triple lock -- a UN mandate , Government approval , D ? il approval through a resolution -- prevents Irish participation of more than 12 Irish troops in military peace-keeping operations outside the country , unless all these three ducks are in a row . Last Wednesday , T ? naiste Miche ? l Martin announced that the Government plans to @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ This signals a major change in Irish foreign policy . If , or when , this happens , it will allow the Government to send Irish military personnel wherever , whenever . The upside is that our little country will be seen as the EU compliant member it has always been , part of the whole . The downside -- and this bleak image is not meant to scaremonger -- is that future generations could find themselves peering into EU-stamped body bags identifying their Irish war dead . Speaking in the D ? il , Miche ? l Martin said : " It would therefore make sense , I believe , to amend our existing legislation in a manner which would allow us to respond to crisis situations with more agility , and where in making these important decisions , we are not surrendering our sovereignty . " ' Agility ' ? And as for ' sovereignty ' ? That will be handed over to the EU while he cites Russia 's UN Security Council permanent member 's role as dictating our foreign policy.The Journal reported : " In 2013 @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ Defence Minister Alan Shatter , argued that the positives of the system outweighed the negatives , recommending to retain the policy , and cited ' substantial public support ' . " In 2014 , the then-Defence Minister Simon Coveney noted that keeping the triple lock system could result in a situation ' where there is a pressing moral or security imperative and overwhelming international support ' for a military response , but that a UN sanction might not be forthcoming as a veto could be exercised by a permanent member of the Security Council . " A change to the system was mooted by Coveney in 2022 after Fine Gael members voted in favour of such a move at its annual conference . At the time , Coveney said he did n't see a move away from the triple lock as ' radical change ' . " The Green Party has also dropped its support for the triple lock.Following fierce political and public debate and criticism , the Consultative Forum on International Security Policy Forum ( examining Ireland 's place in global foreign affairs ) took place in June in @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ that the country 's current defence strategy will still ' pose challenges ' . It also noted that there was no mandate from the public to change the country 's policy of neutrality.Essentially , the Consultative Forum and Miche ? l Martin have bookended the conversation on the triple lock , which is now over . Last month , the EU held its first live military exercise -- an effort to show the world it 's a serious security and defense player that can operate without NATO . The exercise involved 2,800 personnel from nine countries -- Austria , Spain , France , Hungary , Ireland , Italy , Malta , Portugal and Romania.On November 14 , the 27 EU Ministers of Defence , including Miche ? l Martin , approved the 2023 EU Capability Development , a baseline for EU-wide defence planning and EU defence-related initiatives . This chipping away at the country 's neutrality is neither honest nor acceptable . It is a political cynical exercise .
